ATTACHMENT B 
APPENDIX A 
DECOMMISSIONING TRUST FUND GUIDELINES 
I. 
Purpose and Scope 
Entergy Arkansas, Inc. ("EAI") provides for the decommissioning of its Arkansas 
Nuclear One Steam Electric Generating Station, Unit Nos. 1 and 2, through three 
external nuclear plant decommissioning trust funds (hereinafter referred to as the 
"Funds"). The purpose of these guidelines is to establish general criteria for the Fund(@, 
the Trustee@), and the Investment Manager@); specific provisions regarding the 
investment of Fund assets; and reporting requirements. 
11. 
General Provisions 
A. 
Each Fund must meet the following criteria: 
1. 
The Fund must be an external trust fund in the United States, established 
pursuant to a written trust agreement, that is'independent of EAI, its 
parent, subsidiaries, affiliates or associates. 
2. 
Neither EAI nor its parent, subsidiaries, affiliates or associates may serve 
as Trustee or Investment Manager or otherwise engage in day-to-day 
management of the Fund or mandate individual investment decisions. 
3. 
EAI may provide overall investment policy to the Trustee or Investment 
Manager, but such instructions regarding investment policy must be 
provided in writing. 
4. 
The Fund's Investment Manager must exercise the standard of care, 
whether insinvesting or otherwise acting on behalf of the Fund, that a 
prudent investor would use in the same circumstances. The term "prudent 
investor" means a prudent investor as described in Restatement (Third) of 
Trusts $227 - General Standard of Prudent Investment (1992). 
5. 
The Trustee shall have a net worth of at least $100 million. 
The 
Investment Manager shall have a net worth of at least $20 million. In 
calculating the net worth of the Trustee or Investment Manager, the net 
worth of the Trustee's or the Investment Manager's parent corporation 
and/or affiliates may be taken into account only if such entities guarantee 

the Trustee's or the Investment Manager's responsibilities to the Fund. 
6. 
7. 
8. 
9. 
The Trustee or Investment Manager shall keep accurate and detailed 
accounts of all investments, receipts, disbursements and transactions of the 
Fund. All accounts, books and records relating to the Fund shall be open 
to inspection and audit at reasonable times by EAI or its designee or by 
the Commission or its designee. Each party must notify the other prior 
to performing any such inspection or audit. The Commission may direct 
EAI to conduct an audit or inspection. 
Absent the express authorization of the Commission, no part of the assets 
of the Fund may be used for, or diverted to, any purpose other than to 
fund the costs of decommissioning the nuclear power plant to which the 
Fund relates, and to pay administrative costs and other incidental 
expenses, including taxes, of the Fund. 
If the Fund balances exceed the amount actually expended for 
decommissioning after decommissioning has been completed, EAI shall 
return the excess USC-jurisdictional amount to ratepayers, in a manner 
the Commission determines. 
Except for investments tied to market indices or other mutual or common 
trust funds, the Investment Manager shall not invest in any securities of 
EAI or in any securities of EM'S parent, subsidiaries, affiliates, 'or 
associates. 
10. 
In order to maximize after-tax real returns on Fund assets, EAI, the 
Trustee, and the Investment Manager shall take maximum advantage of 
tax deductions and credits, when it is consistent with sound business and 
investment practices to do so. 
11. 
EAI shall deposit, in accordance with the provisions of its approved rate 
Rider M26, all amounts included in APSC-jurisdictional rates to fund 
nuclear power plant decommissioning. 
B. 
The establishment, organization, and maintenance of the Funds shall not relieve 
EAI or its subsidiaries, affiliates or associates of any obligations they may have 
as to the decommissioning of AN0 1 and AN0 2. It is not the responsibility of 
the Trustee or Investment Manager to ensure that the amount of monies that a 
Fund contains is adequate to pay for decommissioning of AN0 1 and AN0 2. 
C. 
These guidelines apply to both the "qualified" (under Internal Revenue Code 
section 468A or any successor section) and the non-qualified Funds. 
-2- 

D. 
EAI must regularly supply to each Fund’s Investment Manager, and regularly 
update, essential information about the nuclear unit covered by the Trust Fund 
Agreement, including its description, location, expected remaining useful life, and 
liquidity needs once decommissioning begins and the timing thereof, and any 
other information that the Fund’s Investment Manager would need to construct 
and maintain, over time, a sound investment plan. 
E. 
EAI shall monitor the performance of all Trustees and Investment Managers of 
the Funds and, when necessary, replace them if they are not properly and 
adequately performing their assigned responsibilities. 
The performance of 
Investment Managers, annually and over three-year rolling periods, shall be 
measured against such appropriate benchmarks as included in the Investment 
Manager Guidelines appended to EM’S Investment Management Agreements. 
Should EAI enter into a contract with any Fund Investment Manager or Fund 
Trustee that is other than an “at-will” contract, the stated term of the contract 
shall be no greater than five years. 
F. 
The Trustee may use Fund assets only to: 
1. 
satisfy the liability of EAI for decommissioning costs of AN0 1 and AN0 
2; and, 
2. 
pay administrative costs and other incidental expenses, including taxes, of 
the Fund. 
G. The Funds may be revocable or irrevocable, but if revocable, the Funds may be 
revoked only with the prior approval of the APSC, and at all times and under all 
circumstances, the assets of the Funds, including all amounts included in M S C - 
Jurisdictional rates to fund nuclear power plant decommissioning and all earnings 
thereon, shall be wholly segregated from any other funds and securities of EAI 
or its parent, subsidiaries, affiliates, or associates, and shall be used only for the 
purposes contemplated in paragraph II(F) hereof. 
H. 
Before the hiring of an investment manager or trustee, EAI shall actively solicit 
competitive proposals for such services from qualified investment managers and 
trustees on a nondiscriminatory basis. The parties from whom proposals are 
sought may be limited by reasonable minimum requirements as to expertise, 
experience, financial strength, and other pertinent factors. In the event that 
unusual circumstances arise, EAI shall evaluate the risk of these circumstances 
against the requirements of this paragraph and shall deviate therefrom only when 
deviation from the requirements of this paragraph shall avert imminent threat or 
jeopardy to the Funds, or their earnings. Such deviation shall be substantiated 
by testimony filed in the docket. 
-3- 

m. Specific Provisions Regarding the Investment of Fund Assets 
A. 
The portfolio may be comprised of a combination of taxable and tax-exempt 
securities. 
The primary investment objectives include preservation of 
accumulated principal; therefore, foreign investments, futures and derivatives, 
real estate, limited partnerships, penny stocks, junk bonds and any investment 
which would similarly put the principal at risk, are expressly prohibited, except 
that index futures may be used on a short-term basis by a mutual or common trust 
fund as an operating procedure to reduce the cash drag on the Fund. 
B. 
As the time for decommissioning nears, assets should be phased out of equity 
investments and into less volatile and more conservative investments. 
C. 
Fixed income securities will meet the following criteria: 
1. 
The Investment Manager shall maintain a prudent mix between general 
obligation and revenue municipal bonds. 
2. 
The Investment 
Manager 
shall 
exercise prudent 
geographical 
diversification of municipal securities and no more than 20% of the 
portfolio’s market value shall be municipal securities from one state. 
No more than 10% of the portfolio’s market value may be invested in any 
one issuer. 
3. 
4. 
No more than 5 % of the portfolio’s market value may be invested in any 
one issue. 
5 . . 
There is no limitation on holdings of U.S. government securities. 
6. 
The market value of the corporate bonds of any one industry shall not 
exceed 20% of the market value of the portfolio. 
7. 
The average rating of all issuers shall not be lower than the equivalent of 
an A2 or A from Moody’s or Standard and Poors. Up to 10% of the 
portfolio may be rated Baa/BBB. 
No issuer shall be rated below 
Baa/BBB. If the ratings of an issue are not equivalent between Moody’s 
and Standard and Poors, the lower rating will be used for the purpose of 
applying these criteria. If a security falls below Baa/BBB, the Investment 
Manager should immediately notify the Corporate Finance Department of 
Entergy Services, Inc. in writing of the new rating and the Investment 
Manager’s recommendation regarding the security. U. S. government 
bills, notes and bonds shall be deemed to be rated AAA for the purpose 
of applying these criteria. 
-4- 

8. 
Due to the nature of the Funds, all issues held in the portfolio must have 
liquid, available markets. Short-term liquid investments may be in t h e 
deposits or demand deposits at U.S. banks or insured U.S. credit unions. 
"Overnight" cash will be invested in the Short Term Investment Fund 
account of the custodian bank. Without prior written approval from EM, 
short-term liquidity investments should not exceed 10% of the portfolio. 
IV. 
Reporting Requirements 
A. 
EM shall file with the Commission, within sixty (60) days after the end of each 
quarter, a copy of the quarterly performance reports furnished to EAI by the 
Fund Trustees, except that fourth quarter reports containing the annual report of 
the Trustees must be submitted to the Commission within ninety (90) days after 
the end of the calendar year, in accordance with subparagraph B hereof. 
B. 
EM shall file with the Commission by October 15, 1996, and by March 31 of 
each year thereafter, a copy of the annual reports prepared by the Funds' 
Trustees, which show for the previous calendar year: 
1. 
Fund assets and liabilities at the beginning of the period; 
2. 
Activity of the Fund during the period, including amounts received from 
EN, purchases and sales of investments, gains and losses from investment 
activity, earnings on Fund investments, disbursements from the Fund for 
decommissioning activity and payment of Fund expenses, including taxes; 
and, 
3. 
Fund assets and liabilities at the end of the period. The report should not 
include the liability for decommissioning. 
4. 
If an independent public accountant has expressed an opinion on the report 
or any portion of the report, then that opinion must accompany the report. 
C. 
Additionally, by October 15, 1996, and by March 31 of each year thereafter, to 
the extent that such information is not contained in the annual reports or the 
fourth quarter performance reports prepared by the Funds' Trustees, EAI shall 
file with the Commission the following information: 
1. 
Identification of all Trustees and Investment Managers (names, addresses, 
phone numbers, and the responsibilities of each). 
2. 
A general statement of the primary factors considered in selecting Trustees 
and Investment Managers. 
-5- 

3. 
Detail of fees (including expense reimbursements) paid to Trustees and 
Investment Managers. 
4. 
Pre and after tax rates of return during the year for each Fund as a whole 
and for each major asset category (Le., for equity and for fixed income 
investments). 
5 . 
Pre and after tax annualized rates of return during the most recent three- 
year period for each Fund as a whole and for each major asset category 
(Le., for equity and for fmed income investments). 
6. 
A comparison of the rates of return achieved by each Fund and by each 
major asset category (Le., by equity and by fixed income investments), 
during the most recent year and during the most recent three-year period, 
with appropriate benchmarks referenced in II(E) above. 
7. 
For each Fund, the projected rate of return for the most recent year, based 
on WEFA projections reflected in Rider M26, will be re-weighted by the 
actual average asset allocation during the year, and will be compared with 
the actual rate of return achieved by each Fund. 
8. 
A narrative description of EAI’s asset allocation targets and investment 
strategy for its Funds, and the basis for that strategy. 
9. 
A description of any changes in the asset allocation targets and investment 
strategy during the year, and the reason for the change. 
10. 
A description of any changes during the prior year in the identity of the 
Trustees or Investment Managers of the Funds, and a description of the 
procedure used in selecting new Trustees or Investment Managers, if any 
were selected during the prior year. 
D . 
Proprietary or confidential information provided by EAI to the APSC, including, 
without limitation, information regarding the fees paid to Trustees and Investment 
Managers, shall be provided subject to the terms of a Protective Order adequate 
to protect the proprietary and confidential status of such information. 
E. 
All Trustee and Investment Management Agreements shall be filed with the 
Commission within 15 days of execution. 
-6- 

APPENDIX B 
REQUIRED FILINGS 
1. 
All Trustee and Investment Management Agreements and the Callan Study which 
supports the current investment strategy. 
2. 
All trust fund reports, specifically the Quarterly Summary Statement, as required by 
Order No. 8. 
3. 
Testimony specifically identifying and substantiating the current asset allocation and the 
current investment strategy for the investing of all the funds. 
4. 
Testimony delineating the criteria utilized in the selection of the Mellon Index Fund and 
supporting the decision to use the Mellon Index Fund. 
5 . 
Testimony identifying and substantiating changes in Trustees, Investment Managers, and 
investment instruments since the repeal of the "Black Lung" restrictions.
